turnaround_reason: Everforth (the former ASGN, rebranded and re-tickered on 2026-04-24) is the 4th-largest US IT staffing firm; the stock was beaten to ~$16.9 in a soft IT-hiring cycle and has since recovered to ~$32.58, a cyclical staffing-demand turnaround wrapped in a rebrand.
bullish_points: Profitable and cheap: trailing P/E 16.8, forward P/E 7.6, EV/EBITDA 7.8, P/B 0.74, EV/revenue 0.67 on ~$4B revenue
Heavy, clustered insider buying in April 2026 at $18-22 across 10+ directors/officers — now well in the money, a strong bottom signal
$1B buyback authorized (~vs $1.34B market cap) provides a floor and EPS tailwind
Federal Government segment (ECS) adds a less-cyclical, backlog-driven revenue stream
FCF $214M and a recent Q2 EPS beat (+11%) suggest the earnings trough may be in
bearish_points: Stock has already nearly doubled off the low; the easy cyclical rebound is largely priced
Analyst mean target $27.50 sits BELOW the ~$32.58 price — the tape has run ahead of sell-side estimates
Revenue still declining (-1.3%); IT staffing demand recovery is not yet confirmed in the top line
Listed options are effectively illiquid (sampled ATM IV ~0), so this is a spot-only vehicle
Rebrand is cosmetic — it doesn't change the cyclical staffing fundamentals
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings showing staffing demand inflecting back to growth, plus buyback execution
suggested_trade: Spot only, modest size; wait for a pullback toward the 200-day or add on a growth-confirming Q3 print rather than chasing after the ~2x move
key_risk: IT hiring stays soft and revenue keeps declining, so the multiple re-rates back down after outrunning analyst targets
would_skip_if: You require the top line to actually be growing before paying up, given the price is already above consensus targets
